content: Spouses married in 1990 under statutory community property regime. Husband purchased land jointly with third party in November 2002, after wife filed for separation (July 2002) but before final judgment (June 2008). Husband subsequently donated his share to his mother, who then entered division agreement with co-owner. Articles 177, 180, 184, 191 Italian Civil Code governing statutory community property, its dissolution, spousal consent requirements, and voidability of unauthorized dispositions. the interpretative issue is Whether community property dissolves upon presidential separation order (Art. 708 CCP) or upon final separation judgment, affecting whether the 2002 purchase fell within the marital estate. Supreme Court precedent establishes dissolution occurs ex nunc only upon final separation judgment. Presidential orders are provisional and do not dissolve community property. The 2002 purchase therefore fell within the marital estate. Consequently, the 2005 donation executed unilaterally without spousal consent was voidable under Art. 184 (action timely filed within one-year limitation). The donation's retroactive annulment rendered the subsequent division ineffective under the principle nemo plus iuris - the mother lacked ownership rights to transfer.
